title: A crash in a runner's own half-built probe is logged on that runner's task instead of filed as an app crash
goal: When a runner tests unfinished work and the test copy of the app crashes, the crash watcher files it as a new app crash, so the dashboard shows crash tasks for bugs that never reached the app and a later runner spends a whole turn proving that. The watcher should tell a crash in a half-built test copy apart from one in landed code.
notes: Happened twice in a week, both closed as runner diagnostics after a full runner turn each: the-app-crashed-in-run-pickuptile (2026-11-11 20:22, throwaway NSStringFromClass loop in pickUpTile) and the-app-crashed-in-documentaudioengine-play (2026-11-13 11:40, two voices wired straight into one AVAudioUnitTimePitch, fixed before 0c0b3edf8 landed). Evidence: queue/loop.log around line 150405 shows '[crash-watch] crash probe 2026-11-13 11:40:48 ... filed the-app-crashed-in-documentaudioengine-play' right after the playback-speed runner exited, and the same runner's transcript a few hundred lines earlier says 'The probe crashed in the new sound path at a non-1x speed ... the time-pitch unit has one input'. The pickuptile task's log proposed this fix ('if it happens again, stamp the probe build with the git tree state'). Sketch: Scripts/probe-app.sh writes {binaryUUID, head, dirty, task} beside the bundle (or into Info.plist); queue/bin/crash-watch.mjs reads the report's slice_uuid, and on a dirty build calls queue.mjs log <task> instead of addjson. A third, the-app-crashed-in-nsapplication-photonz-nexteve, is open and being asked the same question.
acceptance: A probe build records whether it was built from the committed tree or from uncommitted changes (and which task was running)
crash-watch logs a crash from an uncommitted-build probe on the task that was running, and does not file a new task for it

A crash in a probe that a runner had a debugger attached to (lldb -p, or the app's own main appearing mid-stack above system frames) is also logged on the running task rather than filed, even when the probe was built from the committed tree
A crash from a probe built from the committed tree is still filed exactly as today
A drill or test shows both cases

log.note: Another likely case, 2026-11-22: crash-watch filed the-app-crashed-in-static-photonzapp-main from a probe that ran 03:08 to 03:12 during long-edit pass 27, built from that runner's unfinished tree. Triage moved it to p2 as a question.

A third kind, 2026-11-22 03:12 (the-app-crashed-in-static-photonzapp-main): a probe built from the COMMITTED tree that crashed because the runner had lldb attached (pass 27's /tmp/pz27-nodes-run.sh: breakpoints in SwiftUI's focus walk, EvaluateExpression in a callback, lldb killed by perl alarm 250 mid-expression). A dirty-tree stamp would have filed it anyway. Tell-tales in the report: the executable's own Photonz_main/$main frames appear in the MIDDLE of the stack, above system frames (lldb's injected-call return address), and the crash time matches a runner command with 'lldb -p'. Took a full runner turn to rule out (3 rounds of pass 27's walks, no recurrence).
